verdict.rationale: AMD documents a substantial first-party developer stack for this chip: official Windows 11, RHEL and Ubuntu support, the Ryzen AI Software SDK (ONNX Runtime with the Vitis AI EP), Quark quantization, the AI Analyzer, xrt-smi and Lemonade, plus model-deployment guidance. A hands-on user confirms llama.cpp works on Strix Halo. However, the evidence covers AI inference tooling only, not the broader architecture as a tier-one compile target; missing for 10: evidence of mature compiler toolchains for the CPU/iGPU, official general (non-AI) optimization guides, and independent confirmation that OS and tooling ecosystems treat it as tier one.

support.subject: As a developer, this architecture is a first-class development target — mature compilers, official optimization guidance, and an OS and tooling ecosystem that treats it as tier one

citations.quote: Windows 11 - 64-Bit Edition , RHEL x86 64-Bit , Ubuntu x86 64-Bit
This allows developers to build and deploy models trained in PyTorch or TensorFlow and run them directly on laptops powered by Ryzen AI using ONNX Runtime and the Vitis™ AI Execution Provider (EP).
AMD Quark is a comprehensive cross-platform deep learning toolkit designed to simplify and enhance the quantization of deep learning models.
AMD AI Analyzer is a tool that supports analysis and visualization of model compilation and inference on Ryzen AI.
The xrt-smi utility is a command-line interface to monitor and manage the NPU integrated AMD CPUs.
I've mostly been running QWEN-3.6-35B-A3B at Q8 and QWEN-3.5-122B-A10B at Q4 with Q8 kv-cache on llama.cpp.
